ac:rich-text-body.p: Every Wave traverses 4 macro-phases. This page is the visual control room: each Wave's current phase is tracked in the Wave Scope page, and the embedded views below show what's in flight.

ac:rich-text-body.p: Sprint & Repository association. The Wave Scope page has dedicated fields for Sprint ID · Sprint URL · Linked Jira Epic · Repository · Branch · Release Tag. These are filled during Shape & Align (when the Wave is decomposed) and updated through Execute & Evolve (as work progresses). The fields are always present on the Wave Scope but can be left empty for very small Waves.

h2: The visual: from artifact to business intent
p: The macro-phases form a continuous loop:

ac:structured-macro.ac:plain-text-body: ┌─── 1. Instruct & Scope ────┐ │ │ │ ▼ │ │ 2. Shape & Align ──┐ │ │ │ │ │ │ ▼ │ │ │ 3. Execute & Evolve │ │ │ │ │ │ │ ▼ │ │ │ 4. Learn & Adapt ───┘ │ │ │ │ └───┘ back to next Wave

p: Live view of where every active Wave sits in the lifecycle. Updated automatically as Wave Captains move their Wave forward.

ac:rich-text-body.p: To filter Waves by macro-phase, use the page properties report — see for setup.

p: The 7 sub-phases give granularity for daily work. The 4 macro-phases give a shared language for cross-team and executive conversations:

ul.li: For the Wave Captain — "We're in Execute & Evolve" is enough context to communicate status. No need to dive into the sub-phase.
For sponsors and stakeholders — The 4 phases mirror common product lifecycle vocabulary (discover → design → build → learn). Easy to align with executive language.
For governance reviews — Auditors can see at a glance whether a Wave is still in flight (phases 1-3) or in adaptation (phase 4). Compliance triggers differ per phase.
For continuous improvement — Phase 4 (Learn & Adapt) is what makes D-POAF® a living framework rather than a one-shot pipeline. It feeds intent and governance back into the next Wave.

p: The 4 macro-phases are normatively defined in the D-POAF® Canonical Specification v1.1, §4.1 (Lifecycle Macro-Phases — Wave Lifecycle Core).
